OPERATIVE REPORT

PATIENT NAME: Priya Sharma
MRN: BWH-87654321
DATE OF BIRTH: 08/12/1975 (Age: 48)
ADDRESS: 1234 Commonwealth Ave, Apt 5B, Boston, MA 02135
PHONE: (617) 555-0198

PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:
1. Symptomatic uterine fibroids
2. Menorrhagia refractory to medical management

POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:
Same as preoperative

PROCEDURE PERFORMED:
Robotic-assisted laparoscopic myomectomy with da Vinci Xi Surgical System (SN: XI-45678)

SURGEON: Dr. Olivia Bennett
ASSISTANT: Dr. Jamal Williams
ANESTHESIOLOGIST: Dr. Mei Lin Chen
LOCATION: Brigham and Women's Hospital, Main OR #4

DATE OF PROCEDURE: 02/28/2023

INDICATIONS:
48-year-old female with symptomatic fibroids measuring up to 8 cm on recent US, causing bulk symptoms and heavy menstrual bleeding. Failed medical management with oral contraceptives and tranexamic acid. Desires fertility preservation.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
After informed consent, patient was brought to OR and placed in dorsal lithotomy position. General anesthesia was induced without complications. Abdomen was prepped and draped in sterile fashion. Foley catheter was placed. Using the da Vinci Xi system, five trocars were placed under direct visualization: one 12 mm umbilical port, two 8 mm robotic ports in bilateral lower quadrants, one 5 mm assistant port in left upper quadrant, and one 5 mm liver retractor port in right upper quadrant.

Uterus was noted to have three intramural fibroids measuring 8 cm (posterior), 5 cm (anterior), and 3 cm (fundal). Vasopressin (20 units in 100 mL NS) was injected into myometrium around fibroids. Fibroids were enucleated using monopolar scissors and bipolar forceps. Myometrial defects were closed in three layers using 0-Vicryl interrupted sutures. Hemostasis was achieved. Specimen was morcellated using contained power morcellation system (Karl Storz Rotocut G1, SN: RC-78901) and removed through umbilical port site.

Estimated blood loss: 300 mL
Fluids: 1500 mL LR
Urine output: 200 mL
Specimens: Multiple fragments of fibroid tissue sent to pathology
Complications: None

POSTOPERATIVE PLAN:
1. Transfer to PACU with stable vital signs
2. Advance diet as tolerated
3. IV acetaminophen and ketorolac for pain control
4. Discharge tomorrow if meets criteria
5. Follow-up in 2 weeks with Dr. Bennett

DICTATED BY: Dr. Olivia Bennett
DICTATION TIME: 02/28/2023 16:30
SIGNED BY: Dr. Olivia Bennett, 02/28/2023 17:15

PATHOLOGY REPORT (PRELIMINARY):
Gross examination shows multiple fragments of whorled, firm tan-white tissue consistent with leiomyomata. Final diagnosis pending microscopic examination.

PATHOLOGIST: Dr. Samuel Goldstein
DATE: 02/28/2023

ASSISTANT: Dr. Olivia Chen

OPERATING ROOM: OR 4, Johns Hopkins Hospital
DATE OF PROCEDURE: 11/28/2022

INDICATIONS:
64-year-old female with recurrent episodes of RUQ pain, nausea, and vomiting. Ultrasound demonstrated multiple gallstones with positive sonographic Murphy's sign. Patient was evaluated in the Johns Hopkins General Surgery Clinic on 11/15/2022 and deemed appropriate for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
After informed consent was obtained, the patient was brought to the operating room and placed supine on the operating table. General anesthesia was induced without complications. The abdomen was prepped and draped in sterile fashion. A Veress needle was introduced in the infraumbilical position and pneumoperitoneum was established using the Stryker Endoscopy Insufflation System (Model: 1488, SN: SEIS-78234). Intra-abdominal pressure was maintained at 15 mmHg.

Four ports were placed:
1. 10 mm infraumbilical port for 30-degree laparoscope
2. 5 mm epigastric port
3. 5 mm right midclavicular port
4. 5 mm right anterior axillary port

The gallbladder was identified and carefully dissected from the liver bed using the Medtronic LigaSure device (Model: LF1537, SN: ML-45912). The cystic duct and artery were clearly identified, clipped with titanium clips, and divided. An intraoperative cholangiogram was performed through the cystic duct using the GE OEC 9900 Elite Mobile C-Arm (SN: GE-67890), which showed normal biliary anatomy without filling defects or obstruction.

The gallbladder was removed from the abdomen through the umbilical port site. Hemostasis was confirmed. The fascial defect at the umbilical port site was closed with 0-Vicryl suture. Skin incisions were closed with 4-0 Monocryl subcuticular sutures. Steri-Strips and sterile dressings were applied.

ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS: 25 mL
SPECIMENS: Gallbladder sent to pathology
DRAINS: None
COMPLICATIONS: None

The patella was resurfaced with a polyethylene component. The knee was thoroughly irrigated and the arthrotomy was closed in layers with #1 Vicryl, 2-0 Vicryl, and staples for skin.

**Patient Name:** Priya Sharma  
**Age:** 38  
**MRN:** BWH-45678901  
**Hospital:** Brigham and Women's Hospital  
**Address:** 123 Maple Street, Apt 4B, Boston, MA 02115

**Procedure:** Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy  
**Date of Surgery:** 10/12/2023  
**Surgeon:** Dr. Andrew Bennett  
**Assistant Surgeon:** Dr. Naomi Okoro  
**Anesthesiologist:** Dr. Carlos Mendez  
**Equipment Used:** Stryker 1588 HD Camera System (SN: ST-1588-7890), Karl Storz Laparoscopic Instruments  

**INDICATIONS:**  
38-year-old female with symptomatic cholelithiasis presenting with recurrent episodes of RUQ pain, nausea, and vomiting. Ultrasound confirmed multiple gallstones without evidence of cholecystitis. Patient failed conservative management and elected for surgical intervention.  

**PREOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:**  
Symptomatic cholelithiasis  

**POSTOPERATIVE DIAGNOSIS:**  
Same  

**PROCEDURE DETAILS:**  
After informed consent was obtained, the patient was brought to the operating room and placed in supine position. General anesthesia was administered without complications. The abdomen was prepped and draped in sterile fashion.  

A 12 mm infraumbilical incision was made and Veress needle inserted to establish pneumoperitoneum to 15 mmHg. A 10 mm trocar was then placed under direct vision. The Stryker 1588 HD Camera System provided excellent visualization. Three additional 5 mm ports were placed in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant.  

The gallbladder was identified and carefully dissected from the liver bed using a combination of blunt dissection and electrocautery. The cystic duct and artery were identified, clipped with Hem-o-lok clips, and divided. The gallbladder was removed from the liver bed without complication and extracted through the umbilical port site.  

The abdomen was irrigated and hemostasis confirmed. All instruments were removed under direct vision. The pneumoperitoneum was evacuated and port sites were closed with 4-0 Vicryl sutures. Sterile dressings were applied.  

**ESTIMATED BLOOD LOSS:** <25 mL  
**SPECIMENS:** Gallbladder sent to pathology  
**COMPLICATIONS:** None  
**DRAINS:** None  

**POSTOPERATIVE PLAN:**  
- Discharge home same day with prescriptions for acetaminophen and ibuprofen  
- Follow-up with Dr. Bennett in 7-10 days  
- Call office at (617) 555-0193 with any concerns

Laparoscopic-assisted vaginal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy

INDICATIONS:
The patient is a 58-year-old perimenopausal female with a history of symptomatic uterine fibroids causing significant menorrhagia, pelvic pressure, and anemia (Hgb 9.2 g/dL). Failed medical management with oral contraceptives and tranexamic acid. After discussion of risks, benefits, and alternatives, patient elected to proceed with definitive surgical management.

DESCRIPTION OF PROCEDURE:
After obtaining informed consent, the patient was brought to the operating room and placed in dorsal lithotomy position. General endotracheal anesthesia was administered without complications. A time-out was performed confirming correct patient, procedure, and site. The abdomen and vagina were prepped and draped in sterile fashion.

A 10 mm umbilical port was placed using open Hasson technique. Pneumoperitoneum was established to 15 mmHg. Three additional 5 mm ports were placed under direct visualization in the bilateral lower quadrants and suprapubic region. Diagnostic laparoscopy revealed an enlarged uterus measuring approximately 14 weeks size with multiple subserosal fibroids. No evidence of endometriosis or other pelvic pathology.

The round ligaments were cauterized and divided bilaterally. The infundibulopelvic ligaments were skeletonized, doubly ligated with Hem-o-lok clips, and divided. The bladder was carefully dissected off the lower uterine segment. The uterine arteries were skeletonized and ligated at their origin using bipolar cautery. The uterosacral and cardinal ligaments were divided sequentially.

The colpotomy was performed laparoscopically, and the specimen was delivered vaginally. The vaginal cuff was closed in running fashion with 0-Vicryl. Hemostasis was confirmed laparoscopically. The pelvis was irrigated and dried. All ports were removed under direct visualization. The umbilical fascial defect was closed with 0-Vicryl suture. Skin incisions were closed with 4-0 Monocryl.

General endotracheal anesthesia

None

The uterus was enlarged to approximately 12-week size with multiple intramural and subserosal fibroids. No evidence of malignancy.

The patient was placed in dorsal lithotomy position. A Foley catheter was inserted. The abdomen was prepped and draped in sterile fashion. Pneumoperitoneum was established using a Veress needle. - 5 mm right anterior axillary port

The gallbladder was removed from the liver bed using electrocautery and extracted through the umbilical port site in an Endo Catch bag.

The operative field was inspected and hemostasis confirmed. The trocars were removed under direct visualization. The fascia at the umbilical port site was closed with 0 Vicryl suture. Skin incisions were closed with 4-0 Monocryl subcuticular sutures and Dermabond.

Gallbladder sent to pathology

INDICATIONS:
The patient is a 42-year-old female with a 6-month history of recurrent right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and fatty food intolerance. Ultrasound on 04/12/2023 demonstrated multiple gallstones with gallbladder wall thickening. The patient was evaluated in the General Surgery clinic at Massachusetts General Hospital on 04/18/2023 and elected to proceed with surgery.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
The patient was brought to the operating room on 05/05/2023 and placed supine on the operating table. General anesthesia was induced without complications. The abdomen was prepped and draped in sterile fashion. A Veress needle was inserted at the umbilicus and pneumoperitoneum was established using the Stryker Endoscopy Insufflator (Model: 1488, SN: SEI-45678). A 10 mm trocar was placed at the umbilicus and the 30-degree laparoscope was introduced.

Under direct visualization, three additional ports were placed:
1. 5 mm epigastric port
2. 5 mm right midclavicular port
3. 5 mm right anterior axillary port

The gallbladder was identified with dense omental adhesions to the anterior abdominal wall. These were carefully lysed using the Medtronic LigaSure device (Model: LF1537). The cystic duct and artery were identified and carefully dissected. An intraoperative cholangiogram was performed using the C-arm fluoroscopy unit, which demonstrated normal biliary anatomy without filling defects or obstruction.

The cystic duct was doubly clipped with Hem-o-lok clips and divided. The cystic artery was similarly clipped and divided. The gallbladder was dissected from the liver bed using electrocautery and removed through the umbilical port site. The gallbladder was opened and confirmed to contain multiple pigmented stones.

The operative field was inspected and hemostasis was confirmed. The trocars were removed under direct visualization. The fascia at the umbilical port site was closed with 0 Vicryl suture. The skin at all port sites was closed with 4-0 Monocryl in subcuticular fashion. Dermabond was applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit in stable condition.

SPECIMENS: Uterus with cervix, bilateral fallopian tubes
DRAINS: None
COMPLICATIONS: None

INDICATIONS:
48-year-old female with symptomatic fibroids causing menorrhagia, pelvic pressure, and anemia (Hgb 9.2 g/dL). Failed medical management with oral contraceptives and tranexamic acid. Desires definitive surgical management.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
After informed consent, patient was brought to OR #5 and placed in dorsal lithotomy position. General anesthesia was induced without complications. Patient was prepped and draped in sterile fashion. Foley catheter was placed. Pneumoperitoneum was established using Veress needle technique to 15 mmHg. A Stryker 1588 HD Laparoscopic System (SN: STK-56789) was used for visualization.

- 10 mm umbilical port
- 5 mm right lower quadrant port
- 5 mm left lower quadrant port
- 5 mm suprapubic port

The round ligaments were cauterized and divided bilaterally. The infundibulopelvic ligaments were skeletonized, and the ureters were identified bilaterally. The uterine vessels were skeletonized and sealed using LigaSure device. The bladder was dissected off the lower uterine segment. The cardinal ligaments were divided. The colpotomy was performed laparoscopically. The uterus was delivered vaginally. The vaginal cuff was closed laparoscopically using 0-Vicryl in running fashion. Hemostasis was confirmed. All instruments were removed under direct visualization. Pneumoperitoneum was released. Port sites were closed with 4-0 Monocryl.

Patient was extubated and transferred to PACU in stable condition. Sponge, needle, and instrument counts were correct x2. Estimated blood loss was 250 mL. No complications occurred.

Patient to be admitted overnight for observation. Will continue IV fluids and pain management. Will advance diet as tolerated. Foley to remain in place until morning. Discharge planned for tomorrow if meets criteria.

Symptomatic cholelithiasis with chronic cholecystitis

The patient is a 68-year-old female with severe right knee osteoarthritis who has failed extensive conservative management including physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injections. She has debilitating pain affecting her quality of life and activities of daily living. After thorough discussion of risks and benefits, the patient elected to proceed with total knee arthroplasty.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:
The patient was brought to the operating room and placed supine on the operating table. General anesthesia was administered by Dr. Martinez. The right lower extremity was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. A tourniquet was placed on the proximal thigh and inflated to 300 mmHg.

A standard midline incision was made with a #10 blade, followed by medial parapatellar arthrotomy. The patella was everted and the knee flexed. The Stryker Triathlon cutting guide system was utilized for precise bone cuts. The distal femur was cut in 5° of valgus using the intramedullary guide. The proximal tibia was cut perpendicular to the mechanical axis with 3° of posterior slope using the extramedullary guide.

After appropriate sizing, the femoral component (size 4) and tibial component (size 3) were cemented in place with Palacos bone cement. A 10 mm polyethylene insert was placed. The patella was resurfaced with a 32 mm dome patellar component. The knee was taken through range of motion and found to be stable with excellent tracking.

The wound was irrigated copiously with antibiotic solution. The arthrotomy was closed with #1 Vicryl, subcutaneous tissue with 2-0 Vicryl, and skin with staples. A sterile dressing was applied. The tourniquet was released after 78 minutes of inflation time.

None

None
